objectives.text: Pupils should be able to: find missing numbers in an open sentence;
Pupils should be able to: solve simple related open sentences.
Pupils should be able to: 1. add two whole numbers from 1 to 3 with sum less than 5;
Pupils should be able to: 2. add two or three whole numbers from 1 to 8 with sum not up to 10;
Pupils should be able to: 3. add two or three numbers from 0 to 9 with sum not greater than 18;
Pupils should be able to: 4. add 2-digit whole numbers with sum not greater than 40 without exchanging or renaming;
Pupils should be able to: 5. cross check numeracy in addition is readable.
Pupils should be able to: 1. subtract from whole numbers not greater than 18;
Pupils should be able to: 1. subtract from whole numbers not greater than 9;
Pupils should be able to: 2. crosscheck accuracy in subtraction.
Pupils should be able to: 1. find missing numbers in a statement;
Pupils should be able to: 2. cross-check the correctness of addition in everyday life.
Pupils should be able to: 1. find missing numbers in a statement;
Pupils should be able to: 2. cross-check the correctness of subtraction in everyday life.
Pupils should be able to: collect data on their ages at home and school;
Pupils should be able to: collect data on their heights.
Pupil should be able to: 1.  recognize different denomination of Nigerian coins;
Pupil should be able to: 2.   add coins to obtain sums not exceeding 25k;
Pupil should be able to: 3.  calculate change obtainable from 10k or less;
Pupil should be able to: 4.  trace coins using brown and white papers.
Pupil should be able to: 1.  develop the idea of length;
Pupil should be able to: 2.  compare length of two or three objects;
Pupil should be able to: 3.  order similar objects according to lengths;
Pupil should be able to: 4. measure length and distance in their natural units;
Pupil should be able to: 5. apply the length and ordering of lengths in our environment.
Pupils should be able to: 1. demonstrate knowledge of the idea of time;

Pupils should be able to: 2. mention when certain things are done :
- Home
- School.
1. Compare the weights of some common objects in the school using the terms light and heavy.
Pupils should be able to: 1.  sort out cubes, cuboids, cylinders and spheres;
Pupils should be able to: 2.  identify and name cuboids, cubes, cylinders and spheres;
Pupils should be able to: 3.  distinguish between cuboids and cubes;
Pupils should be able to: 4.  mention solid shapes in homes and environment.
Pupils should be able to: 1.  identify a Square, a Rectangle and a Circle.
Pupils should be able to: 2.  match and name a  square, a rectangle and a Circle.
Pupils should be able to: 3.  distinguish between squares and rectangles.
Pupils should be able to: 4.  mention  square, rectangular and circular shapes in homes.
Pupils should be able to: arrange; numbers 1-5 in order of their magnitudes (quantities)
Pupils should be able to: count correctly up to 5;
Pupils should be able to: identify number of objects in a group or collection;
Pupils should be able to: sort and classify number of objects in a group or collection;
Pupils should be able to: write correctly number 1-5;
Pupil should be able to: read the number 0;
Pupil should be able to: recognize that the symbol 0 stands for nothingness;
Pupil should be able to: Write 0.

Pupil should be able to:
1.  sort and classify numbers of objects in a group or collection;

Pupil should be able to:
2.  identify number of objects in a group or collection;

Pupil should be able to:
3.  Count and read correctly from 1-9;

Pupil should be able to:
4.  write correctly number 6-9;

Pupil should be able to:
5.  arrange the numbers 6-9 in order of their magnitudes (quantities).

Pupil should be able to:
1.  recognize 10 as a group;

Pupil should be able to:
2.  use idea of place value limited to tens and units.
Pupils should be able to: 1. identify and read correctly the numbers 1-99;
Pupils should be able to: 2. write correctly the numbers 1-99.
Pupil should be able to: 1. identify ½ and ¼ using concrete objects and shapes,
Pupils should be able to: 1. Collect data and arrange them in arrays;
Pupils should be able to: 2. Collect data and arrange them in groups such as group of boys and group of  girls;
Pupils should be able to: 1. enumerate the uses of money;
Pupils should be able to: 2. recognize all types of Nigerian coins and bank notes;
Pupils should be able to: 3. change money up to ₦20 into small units and shop with money not greater than ₦20.
Pupils should be able to: 1.  compare their natural units with another e.g. arm‟s length;
Pupils should be able to: 2. identify the differences in arm‟s length and other parts of the body used for measurement;
Pupils should be able to: 3.  use meters and centimetres as standard measuring units;
Pupils should be able to: 4. identify the need for lengths and measurement using standardized units.
Pupils should be able to: give time to the hour and half;
Pupils should be able to: name and arrange days of the week.
1. Pupils should be able to order objects according to their weights.

Pupils should be able to:
1. identify and name objects that could be used for measuring capacity e.g. cups, empty containers buckets etc.;

Pupils should be able to:
2.  order containers based on their capacities.

Pupils should be able to:
1. compare areas of surfaces;

Pupils should be able to:
2. identify the use of standard measuring units;

Pupils should be able to:
1. identify and count the flat faces of a cube and a cuboid;

Pupils should be able to:
2. identify and count the corners of a cube and a cuboid;

Pupils should be able to:
3. identify and count the edges of a cube and cuboid;

Pupils should be able to:
4. identify objects at home that are cuboids and cubes;

Pupils should be able to:
5. identify the curved surfaces of a cylinder;

Pupils should be able to:
6. mention three dimensional objects in their homes that are cylinders and spheres.

Pupils should be able to:

1. identify a square, a rectangle, a circle and a triangle;
Pupils should be able to: 2.  indicate which corner of a        2-dimensional shape is a “square corner”.

Pupils should be able to:
1. add 2-digit numbers without exchanging or renaming;

Pupils should be able to:
2. add 3-digit numbers without exchanging or renaming;

Pupils should be able to:
3. add 2-digit numbers with exchanging or renaming;

Pupils should be able to:
4. add 3 numbers taking two at a time.
Pupils should be able to: 1. subtract 2-digit numbers without exchanging or renaming;
Pupils should be able to: 2. subtract 2-digit numbers with exchanging and renaming;
Pupils should be able to: 3. apply addition and subtraction in everyday activities.
Pupils should be able to: 1. multiply numbers using repeated additions;
Pupils should be able to: 2. apply correctness in multiplications as important in everyday activities.
Pupils should be able to: find missing numbers in an open sentence;
Pupils should be able to: Solve simple related quantitative aptitude problems.
Pupils should be able to: 1.  count numbers correctly from 1-200;
Pupils should be able to: 2.  identify and read numbers from 1 – 200;
Pupils should be able to: 3. identify order and write numbers up to 200.
Pupils should be able to: 1. divide a collection of concrete objects into two equal parts and four equal parts;
Pupils should be able to: 2. obtain ¾ of a concrete object.
The pupils should be able to: identify the most common features of pictogram (the mode);
The pupils should be able to: mention the usefulness of pictogram (the mode).
The pupils should be able to: read and represent information in pictograms using vertical and horizontal arrangements;
The pupils should be able to: represent information on a pictogram;

Pupils should be able to :
1.  find missing number in an open sentence;

Pupils should be able to :
3.  solve related quantitative aptitude problems.
Pupils should be able to: 1. add 2-digit numbers with exchanging or renaming;
Pupils should be able to: 2. add 3 - digit numbers;
Pupils should be able to: 2. add 3 numbers taking two at a time;
Pupils should be able to: 3. add fractions with the same denominator;
Pupils should be able to: 4. mention the need for correct addition of numbers and fractions in everyday activities.
Pupils should be able to: 1. subtract 2-digit numbers with exchanging or renaming;
Pupils should be able to: 2. subtract 3 - digit numbers;
Pupils should be able to: 3. subtract 3 numbers taking two at a time;
Pupils should be able to: 4. subtract fractions with the same denominator;
Pupils should be able to: 5. mention the need for correct subtraction of numbers and fractions in everyday activities.
Pupils should be able to: 1. multiply from 1 x 1 to 9 x 9
Pupils should be able to: 2. multiply 2-digit number by 1-digit number;
Pupils should be able to: 3. multiply three 1-digit numbers taking two at a time;
Pupils should be able to: 4. carry out correct multiplication in everyday activities.
Pupils should be able to: 1. divide whole numbers not exceeding 48 by 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 without remainder;
Pupils should be able to: 2. express whole numbers not exceeding 48 as products of factors;
Pupils should be able to: 3. find a missing factor in a given numbers;
Pupils should be able to: 4. distinguish between factors and multiples;
Pupils should be able to: 5. carry out correct division in everyday activities.

Pupils should be able to:
1. change money not exceeding ₦20 into smaller units;

Pupils should be able to:
2. shop effectively with money not greater than ₦20 using the idea of addition and subtraction;

Pupils should be able to:
3. perform simple multiplication involving money with product not exceeding ₦20.
Pupils should be able to: find perimeters of regular figures in metres and centimeters by measurement;
Pupils should be able to: identify perimeter of regular shapes in their environment;
Pupils should be able to: measure the length and/or width of room, table, building and straight edged materials, etc.;
Pupils should be able to: mention importance/benefits of standard units of measurement;
Pupils should be able to: compare their non standard measures e.g. arms length;
Pupils should be able to: identify the differences in the non-standard measures;
Pupils should be able to: identify the need for lengths and measurement using standardized units.
Pupils should be able to: use meters and centimeters as standard measuring units;
Pupils should be able to: give dates in day and month;
Pupils should be able to: mention the importance of time in daily life activities.
Pupils should be able to: say time accurately in hours and minutes;
Pupils should be able to: appreciate the need for grams and kilogram as standard units of measure for transactions.
Pupils should be able to: make meaningful comparison of weight of objects like rocks, minerals;
Pupils should be able to: measure weights of objects in grams and kilograms;
Pupils should be able to: 1. identify litre as a unit of measuring capacity;
Pupils should be able to: 2. measure liquid e.g. water using a graduated cylinder up to any stated number of litres;
Pupils should be able to: 3. identify the need for accuracy in measuring liquids e.g. kerosine, water petrol etc.

Pupils should be able to:
1.  identify shapes with line(s) of symmetry;

Pupils should be able to:
2.  identify lines of symmetry in everyday life;

Pupils should be able to:
3. state properties of squares, rectangles and triangles;

Pupils should be able to:
4. identify that some shapes in everyday life are square, rectangular, triangular and circular and therefore see mathematics in everyday life;

Pupils should be able to:
5. distinguish between curves and straight lines;

Pupils should be able to:
6. identify  the presence of straight lines and curves in real life situations;

Pupils should be able to:
7. draw squares, rectangles, triangles and circles.
Pupils should be able to: 1.  count correctly numbers up to 999;
Pupils should be able to: 2.  state the place value of a digit in a 3-digit number;
Pupils should be able to: 4.  order whole numbers and use the symbol <   and   >;
Pupils should be able to: 5.  mention the need for counting and ordering.

Pupils should be able to:
1.  state fraction of a group of concrete objects;

Pupils should be able to:
2.  divide shapes into  ½ , 1/3, ¼ etc.;

Pupils should be able to:
3.  write fractions which have the same value as a given fraction;

Pupils should be able to:
4.  use the symbol <  or > to order fractions.
